pr_title: *: add global variable tidb_schema_version_cache_limit to control infoschema cache size
pr_body: ### What problem does this PR solve? Issue Number: close #46524 Problem Summary: add global variable tidb_schema_version_cache_limit to control infoschema cache size and add/refine metric. ### What is changed and how it works? To fix #46524, we can simply enlarge the info-scheme cache capacity from 16 to 64. However, in scenarios with a large number of tables, this increases the risk of TiDB OOM. So this PR just add global variable `tidb_schema_version_cache_limit ` to control infoschema cache size and refine metric in grafana to better diagnose this issue later. If you meet issue in #46524 with same root cause, you can enlarge the global variable `tidb_schema_version_cache_limit ` to fix it. ### Check List Tests - [ ] Unit test - [ ] Integration test - [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below) 1. Deploy a TiDB cluster. 2. run stale read load. ``` sysbench --config-file=sysbench.conf mussel_minimal.lua --threads=20 --read_staleness=-5 run ``` 3. run DDL load by [loadgen](https://github.com/crazycs520/loadgen). Following load will use 1 thread to continuously create tables, from t1 to t100000. ``` loadgen bench --sql 'create table t#seq-val (id int key, b int)' --thread=1 --valmin=1 --valmax=100000 --db=test2 ``` 4. check the metrics. - 17:12: Start running stale-read load, and the query QPS is 18000. - 17:14: Start running DDL load, then the query QPS is dropping to 400. From the `Load Schema OPS` metrics, you can see many load snapshot schema OPS, this is what causes QPS to drop. - 17:18: `set @@global. tidb_schema_version_cache_limit=64;`, then the query QPS return to 18000. Side effects - [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU - [x] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory - [ ] Breaking backward compatibility Documentation - N/A ### Release note Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note. ```release-note None ```

comments: Enlarge infoschema cache capacity to 64 can fix this issue: - [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below) 1. Deploy a TiDB cluster. 2. run stale read load. ``` sysbench --config-file=sysbench.conf mussel_minimal.lua --threads=20 --read_staleness=-5 run ``` 3. run DDL load by [loadgen](https://github.com/crazycs520/loadgen). Following load will use 1 thread to continuously create tables, from t1 to t100000. ``` loadgen bench --sql 'create table t#seq-val (id int key, b int)' --thread=1 --valmin=1 --valmax=100000 --db=test2 ``` 4. check the metrics. **Before** The stale-read query QPS is affected by DDL load and is much lower than without DDL load. You can see there are some load snapshot schema ops after start DDL load, this is the main reason cause QPS lower. The DDL OPM metric: **After Change InfoCache capacity to 64** The stale-read query QPS is stable and not affected by DDL load. 5. Check TiDB server memory usage. With running stale-read load and DDL load, I already create 10000 tables before. ```sql information_schema> select count(*) from `TABLES`; +----------+ | count(*) | +----------+ | 10589 | +----------+ ``` And during running stale-read load and DDL load, the TiDB memory is less than before, since without cache miss. **Before**, TiDB need to fetch all schema by snapshot_ts, it will cost more memory. **After Change InfoCache capacity to 64**, the memory usage is more stable and less than before.

review_comments: I don't know if this is a good idea. Because caching cap could easily make OOM, too.
I have tested it with 10000 tables, it doesn't consume much memory.
How about add a global variable to control it?
Ok, I don't change the default value now, I add a global variable to control it.
